To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gp70 surface envelope of FeLV-B and A-MLVs are composed of two domains, VRA and VR, and that each of these domains interacts in a specific way with distinct regions of the receptors, Pit1 and -2.
(i) the gp70 VRA interacts with the receptor's transmembrane region, (ii) the gp70 VRD interacts with the receptor ECD2, and (iii) the gp70 CTD interacts with the receptor CTD.
the VRA and VR regions of FeLV-B and A-ML-V gp70 interact specifically with ECL2, -4, and -5 of their receptors, Pit1 and -2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of residues in the gp70 surface glycoprotein of A-MLVs and FeLVs that interact with their respective cell surface receptors.
the development and application of a comprehensive approach for mapping the interacting surfaces of retrovirus gp70 and their cellular receptors.
identifying the specific sites on the surface of retroviral envelope glycoproteisms that interact with the surface of their receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
A-MLV gp70 VRA interacts with the Pit2 extracellular loops 2 and 4, whereas FeLV-B gp90 VRA interacts with Pit1 ELC4 and -5.

FeLV-B and A-MLVs use the phosphate symporters as receptors and that the VRA and VRBs of gp70 interact with distinct regions of ECLs 4, 5, and 2 of the receptors, thereby allowing for a highly specific interaction.
the FeLV-B gp 70 surface envelope glyco protein and the A-MLV surface envelope glycoprotein interact in a specific way with their respective receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VRA interacts primarily with the receptor's extracellular loops 2 and 4, whereas the VRB interacts primarily with the loops 4 and/or 5.
the VRA and VRBs of FeLV-B and A-MLVs are functionally divided into three regions that are required for specific interaction with the ECL2, ECL4, and ECL5 regions of the receptors, respectively.

FeLV-B and A-MLVs use their VRA and VRBs to recognize and bind their receptors, Pit1 and -2, respectively, and that Pit1 and Pit-2 interact with their respective gp70s through the ECL4 and ECL5 regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gp70 VRA and VRBs of FeLV-B and A-MLVs are not functionally interchangeable and that the VRA and VRs of these two viruses have distinct roles in their interactions with their receptors.
